label: prop:schur-weyl-eightfold
title: Eightfold-way multiplets via quantum Schur--Weyl duality
html:
The eightfold-way multiplets --- decuplet (\mathbf{10}), octet (\mathbf{8}), and singlet (\mathbf{1}) --- are the quantum Schur--Weyl partners of the Hecke algebra H_3(q) acting on V^{\otimes 3}.

Quantum Schur--Weyl duality (Jimbo [jimbo1986]) states that \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_N) and H_n(q) are mutual centralizers on V^{\otimes n}:

  V^{\otimes n}
  \cong \bigoplus_{\substack{\lambda \vdash n \\ \ell(\lambda) \leq N}}
    V_\lambda^{\mathfrak{gl}_N} \otimes S^\lambda_{H_n(q)},

where \lambda ranges over partitions of n with at most N rows, V_\lambda^{\mathfrak{gl}_N} is the irreducible \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_N)-module labelled by \lambda, and S^\lambda_{H_n(q)} is the irreducible Hecke module (Specht module) labelled by the same partition.

At n = 3 (three-strand braiding) and N = 3 (three-dimensional fundamental representation), the decomposition reads:

  V^{\otimes 3}
  \cong
  \underbrace{V_{(3)}}_{\dim = 10}
    \otimes S^{(3)}
  \;\oplus\;
  \underbrace{V_{(2,1)}}_{\dim = 8}
    \otimes S^{(2,1)}
  \;\oplus\;
  \underbrace{V_{(1,1,1)}}_{\dim = 1}
    \otimes S^{(1,1,1)}.

The dimensions and multiplicities are:

\lambda \vdash 3 \dim V_\lambda^{\mathfrak{gl}_3} \dim S^\lambda_{H_3} Name
(3) 10 (decuplet) 1 symmetric
(2,1) 8 (octet) 2 mixed
(1^3) 1 (singlet) 1 antisymmetric

The total is 10 \cdot 1 + 8 \cdot 2 + 1 \cdot 1 = 27 = 3^3, as required. The Hecke block dimensions (1, 2, 1) are the multiplicities of the flavour irreps, not the irreps themselves.

The N = 3 question. The single-fibre tower of the braiding and Bring's-surface chapters has \dim V = 2 (the standard single-fibre construction yields a quantum form of \mathrm{SU}(2); the Descartes condition \chi(\mathcal{A}) = -6 is compatible with but does not uniquely force N = 2 --- see the \chi-rank audit). The decomposition at N = 2 is:

  V^{\otimes 3}
  \cong V_{(3)} \otimes S^{(3)}
  \;\oplus\;
  V_{(2,1)} \otimes S^{(2,1)},
  \qquad
  4 \cdot 1 + 2 \cdot 2 = 8 = 2^3.

The antisymmetric partition (1^3) is absent (three rows exceed N = 2). No choice of q restores it: the row cap is \ell(\lambda) \leq \dim V, which the single-fibre construction fixes at 2, and the Drinfeld--Jimbo quantisation does not change dimensions.

The obstruction, and what is proved about it. The following are proved:

  • The alternating channel \dim V_{(1^3)} = \binom{N}{3} vanishes if and only if N < 3. This is the obstruction in one line.
  • If the symmetric channel has dimension 10 then N = 3. The implication runs from the decuplet dimension to the flavour dimension, in that direction.
  • A one-dimensional alternating channel likewise pins N = 3.
  • The channel arithmetic closes at both values (8 = 4 + 4 + 0 at N = 2; 27 = 10 + 16 + 1 at N = 3), so the N = 2 deficit sits precisely in the vanishing alternating channel and not in some unaccounted-for piece.

What is not established here. The same caveat applies here as to the q-deformation of the weight lattice above, and it is load-bearing in this one place because N = 3 is the chapter's central open problem. What is proved is the arithmetic of the row cap on the channel dimensions: \dim V_{(1^3)}^{\mathfrak{gl}_N} is taken to be \binom{N}{3} and the reasoning is about \binom{N}{3} alone, every step an elementary binomial identity, a finite check, or linear integer arithmetic. That the hook-content formula gives \dim V_{(1^3)} = \binom{N}{3}, and that the Schur--Weyl row cap is \ell(\lambda) \leq N, are standard and cited, not proved; in particular Worpitzky's identity is not proved here. So the tier is standard mathematics, with a proved arithmetic instance --- not proved in the sense the other proved rows of this chapter use.

The conclusion is nonetheless correct, because the two cited inputs are textbook. The eightfold-way classification is not "approximately available" at N = 2 --- it is structurally unavailable. This is a scope-(b) exclusion, and the invariant justifying it is the Schur--Weyl row cap.

The N = 2 half of the duality is proved. The Jimbo action of H_n(q) on V^{\otimes n} with \dim V = 2 is constructed, and the following are proved over an ordered field at generic q: the induced trace is the Markov trace with z = q^3/(q^2+1); the kernel of the action is exactly the trace radical, i.e. the blocks with three or more rows ; and the image has dimension the Catalan number. Surjectivity onto the \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) commutant is not claimed, and no N \geq 3 action is constructed, so the N = 3 statement above remains cited.

The two pinning results above, from the decuplet and from the singlet, run from an observed channel dimension to N = 3; what the framework requires is N = 3 supplied by a construction. That is the affirmative half, and it remains open.

Therefore, realising the full eightfold way requires N = 3. Within QOU, this N = 3 cannot arise from a single fibre. The remaining construction directions are:

  1. Multi-fibre groupoid: inequivalent fibre objects whose interaction space is three-dimensional (T3b).
  2. Octonionic G_2 stabilizer: the Günaydin--Gürsey \mathbf{7} = \mathbf{1} \oplus \mathbf{3} \oplus \bar{\mathbf{3}} provides a non-self-dual triple from \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} \subset G_2.

Status of the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate. The gate is the requirement that \mathrm{Sym}^2(W) contain no singlet. Its representation-theoretic content is proved: at dimension three, passing the gate forces a complex-type summand, so the icosahedral triple T_1 --- a rotation representation of A_5 \subset \mathrm{SO}(3), hence real --- fails , while the octonionic \mathbf{3} is not excluded, on the decomposition \mathrm{Im}(\mathbb{O}) \cong \mathbb{R} \oplus \mathbb{C}^3 taken from the literature [gunaydin-gursey1973]. That the Günaydin--Gürsey triple is complex type is the cited input, not a proved one, so the octonionic route is not excluded rather than proved to pass. Whether the route yields flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} (not just colour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}}) remains open.
